<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Bank-Owned Life Insurance </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The balance of bank-owned life insurance increased $4.18&#160;million due to an increase in the cash surrender value of underlying policies. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Other Assets </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other assets remained relatively flat from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025, decreasing $999&#160;thousand or less than 1% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025 as prepaid assets decreased $5.06&#160;million, income taxes receivable decreased $2.01&#160;million due to timing differences and core deposit intangibles decreased $1.84&#160;million due to amortization. Partially offsetting these decreases were increases in deferred tax assets of $4.41&#160;million due mainly to the decrease in the fair value of available for sale securities, OREO of $1.53&#160;million and accounts receivable of $1.79&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Deposits </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Deposits represent United&#8217;s primary source of funding. Total deposits at March&#160;31, 2026 increased $59.94&#160;million or less than 1% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025. In terms of composition, noninterest-bearing deposits decreased $163.71&#160;million or 2.49% while interest-bearing deposits increased $223.66&#160;million or 1.09% from December&#160;31, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Noninterest-bearing deposits consist of demand deposit and noninterest bearing money market (&#8220;MMDA&#8221;) account balances. The $163.71&#160;million decrease in noninterest-bearing deposits was due to a $156.81&#160;million decrease in official checks and a $30.41&#160;million decrease in commercial noninterest-bearing deposits. Partially offsetting these decreases was a $38.43&#160;million increase in personal noninterest-bearing deposits and a $5.73&#160;million increase in public funds noninterest-bearing deposits. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest-bearing deposits consist of interest-bearing transactions, regular savings, interest-bearing MMDA, and time deposit account balances. Interest-bearing transaction accounts decreased $39.74&#160;million since <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025 as the result of a $59.80&#160;million decrease in public funds interest-bearing transaction accounts, partially offset by a $16.53&#160;million increase in commercial interest-bearing transaction accounts. Regular savings accounts increased $20.89&#160;million mainly as a result of a $27.94&#160;million increase in personal savings accounts. Interest-bearing MMDAs increased $198.35&#160;million. In particular, personal MMDAs increased $64.96&#160;million while commercial MMDAs and public funds MMDAs increased $114.40&#160;million and $18.99&#160;million, respectively. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Time deposits under $100,000 increased $5.73&#160;million or less than 1% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025. This increase in time deposits under $100,000 was the result of a $26.26&#160;million increase in fixed rate Certificates of Deposits (&#8220;CDs&#8221;) under $100,000 and a $1.77&#160;million increase in Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service (&#8220;CDARS&#8221;) under $100,000, partially offset by a $23.49&#160;million decrease in variable rate CDs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Since <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025, time deposits over $100,000 increased $38.44&#160;million or 1.14% as fixed rate CDs increased $56.84&#160;million. Partially offsetting this increase was a $14.47&#160;million decrease in variable rate CDs and a $5.47&#160;million decrease in CDARS over $100,000. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The table below summarizes the changes by deposit category since <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For a further discussion of borrowings see Notes 8 and 9 to the unaudited Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Accrued Expenses and Other Liabilities </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Accrued expenses and other liabilities at March&#160;31, 2026 increased $24.51&#160;million or 10.11% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025. In particular, income taxes payable increased $30.80&#160;million due to timing differences, business franchise taxes increased $3.03&#160;million, and accrued loan expenses increased $10.43&#160;million. Partially offsetting these increases was a decrease of $16.69&#160;million in incentives payable due to payments. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Shareholders&#8217; Equity </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Shareholders&#8217; equity at March&#160;31, 2026 was $5.49&#160;billion, which was a decrease of $7.86&#160;million or less than 1% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Retained earnings increased $71.03&#160;million or 3.27% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025. Earnings net of dividends for the first three months of 2026 were $71.03&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Accumulated other comprehensive income decreased $10.19&#160;million or 7.33% from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025 due mainly to a decrease of $10.05&#160;million in the fair value of United&#8217;s available for sale investment portfolio, net of deferred income taxes. The fair value of cash flow hedges, net of deferred income taxes, decreased $136&#160;thousand. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Treasury stock increased $70.91&#160;million or 18.59%. During the first quarter of 2026, United repurchased 1,739,501 shares on the open market under a repurchase plan approved by United&#8217;s Board of Directors at a cost of $69.43&#160;million or an average share price of $39.92. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net income for the first quarter of 2026 was $124.20&#160;million as compared to earnings of $84.31&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share were $0.89 for the first quarter of 2026 and $0.59 for the first quarter of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, net income for the fourth quarter of 2025 was $128.83&#160;million or $0.91 per diluted share. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As previously mentioned, United completed its acquisition of Piedmont on January&#160;10, 2025. The financial results of Piedmont are included in United&#8217;s results from the acquisition date. As a result of the acquisition, United recorded acquisition-related costs for the Piedmont merger of $30.04&#160;million, including a provision for credit losses of $18.73&#160;million for purchased <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-PCD</span> loans for the first quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s annualized return on average assets for the first three months of 2026 was 1.49% and return on average shareholders&#8217; equity was 9.08% as compared to 1.06% and 6.47%, respectively, for the first three months of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, United&#8217;s annualized return on average assets for the fourth quarter of 2025 was 1.52% and return on average shareholders&#8217; equity was 9.31%. For the first three months of 2026, United&#8217;s annualized return on average tangible common equity, a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measure, was 14.40%, as compared to 10.61% for the first three months of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, United&#8217;s annualized return on average tangible common equity was 14.86% for the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 increased $22.46&#160;million, or 8.64% from the first quarter of 2025. The increase of $22.46&#160;million in net interest income occurred because total interest income increased $12.28&#160;million while total interest expense decreased $10.18&#160;million from the first quarter of 2025. Net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 decreased $4.94&#160;million, or 1.72%, from the fourth quarter of 2025. The decrease of $4.94&#160;million in net interest income occurred because total interest income decreased $14.12&#160;million while total interest expense decreased $9.18&#160;million from the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The provision for credit losses was $7.78&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to $29.10&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. This decrease in the provision for credit losses was mainly due to the previously mentioned $18.73&#160;million of provision recorded on purchased <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-PCD</span> loans from Piedmont during the first quarter of 2025. The provision for credit losses was $6.78&#160;million for the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the first quarter of 2026, noninterest income increased $4.51&#160;million or 15.26% and $3.13&#160;million or 10.11% from the first quarter and fourth quarter of 2025, respectively. These increases were primarily due to increased fees from brokerage services and net gains on the sale of equity securities in the first quarter of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Noninterest expense for the first quarter of 2026 was flat, decreasing $759&#160;thousand or less than 1% from the first quarter of 2025. The decrease was due mainly to merger-related expenses from the Piedmont acquisition incurred in the first quarter of 2025 being mostly offset by increases in employee compensation and employee benefits expenses during the first quarter of 2026. Noninterest expense for the first quarter of 2026 was also flat from the fourth quarter of 2025, increasing $1.10&#160;million or less than 1% from the fourth quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in employee benefits expense mostly offset by decreases in data processing expense and the amortization of investment tax credits within other expense. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Income taxes increased $9.16&#160;million or 40.49% for the first three months of 2026 as compared to the first three months of 2025 primarily due to higher earnings partially offset by a lower effective tax rate. On a linked-quarter basis, income taxes increased $720&#160;thousand or 2.32% for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to the fourth quarter of 2025 due mainly to a higher effective tax rate partially offset by lower earnings. The effective tax rate was 20.38% and 21.16% for the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate was 19.43% for the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following discussion explains in more detail the consolidated results of operations by major category. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Net Interest Income </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net interest income represents the primary component of United&#8217;s earnings. It is the difference between interest income from earning assets and interest expense incurred to fund these assets. Net interest income is impacted by changes in the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, as well as changes in market interest rates. Such changes, and their impact on net interest income in 2026 and 2025, are presented below. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 was $282.52&#160;million, which was an increase of $22.46&#160;million or 8.64% from the first quarter of 2025. The $22.46&#160;million increase in net interest income occurred because total interest income increased $12.28&#160;million while total interest expense decreased $10.18&#160;million from the first quarter of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 decreased $4.94&#160;million, or 1.72%, from the fourth quarter of 2025. The $4.94&#160;million decrease in net interest income occurred because total interest income decreased $14.12&#160;million while total interest expense decreased $9.18&#160;million from the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the purpose of this remaining discussion, net interest income is presented on a <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> basis to provide a comparison among all types of interest earning assets. The <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> basis adjusts for the <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-favored</span> status of income from certain loans and investments. Although this is a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-GAAP</span> measure, United&#8217;s management believes this measure is more widely used within the financial services industry and provides better comparability of net interest income arising from taxable and <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-exempt</span> sources. United uses this measure to monitor net interest income performance and to manage its balance sheet composition. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">62 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Tax-equivalent</span> net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 was $283.30&#160;million, an increase of $22.46&#160;million or 8.61% from the first quarter of 2025. This increase in <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income was primarily due to an increase in average earning assets, mainly net loans, and a lower average cost of interest-bearing funds, mainly deposits. These increases to <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income were partially offset by an increase in average interest-bearing funds, mainly deposits, and a lower yield on average earning assets, mainly short-term investments. Average earning assets for the first quarter of 2026 increased $1.54&#160;billion or 5.39% from the first quarter of 2025. The increase in average earning assets was due mainly to a $1.38&#160;billion or 5.97% increase in average net loans as well as increases of $107.72&#160;million or 5.05% and $48.75&#160;million or 1.50% in average short-term investments and average investment securities, respectively. Average interest-bearing funds for the first quarter of 2026 increased $1.24&#160;billion or 6.17% from the first quarter of 2025. In particular, average interest-bearing deposits increased $1.25&#160;billion or 6.44% while average short-term borrowings increased $15.35&#160;million or 9.19% and average long-term borrowings decreased $22.64&#160;million or 4.08% from the first quarter of 2025. The average cost of funds for the first quarter of 2026 decreased 36 basis points due primarily to a decrease in interest rates from the first quarter of 2025. Most notably, the cost of average interest-bearing deposits decreased 36 basis points and the cost of average short-term and long-term borrowings decreased 32 basis points and 28 basis points, respectively, from the first quarter of 2025. The average yield on earning assets for the first quarter of 2026 decreased 13 basis points from the first quarter of 2025. In particular, the yield on average short-term investments decreased 76 basis points while the yield on average net loans and average investment securities declined 8 basis points and 15 basis points, respectively. For the first quarter of 2026, interest income and <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income included $7.47&#160;million of acquired loan accretion income as compared to $5.99&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. The net interest margin of 3.80% for the first quarter of 2026 was an increase of 11 basis points from the net interest margin of 3.69% for the first quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On a linked-quarter basis, <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income decreased $4.96&#160;million or 1.72% from the fourth quarter of 2025. The net interest margin was 3.80% and 3.83% for first quarter of 2026 and the fourth quarter of 2025, respectively. The interest rate spread for the first quarter of 2026 increased 2 basis points to 3.06% from the fourth quarter of 2025 due to a 14 basis point decrease in the average cost of funds partially offset by a 12 basis point decrease in the yield on average earning assets. The decrease in the average cost of funds was primarily due to a 14 basis point decrease in the average rate paid on deposits. The decrease in the yield on average earning assets was primarily due to an 11 basis point decrease in the yield on average net loans, a 26 basis point decrease in the yield on average short-term investments and lower acquired loan accretion income. Acquired loan accretion income for the first quarter of 2026 decreased $988&#160;thousand or 11.68% from the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income also includes the impact of acquisition accounting fair value adjustments. The following table provides the discount/premium and net accretion impact to <span style="white-space:nowrap">tax-equivalent</span> net interest income for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, March&#160;31, 2025 and December&#160;31, 2025: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Provision for Credit Losses </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The provision for credit losses was $7.78&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to a provision for credit losses of $29.10&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. On a linked-quarter basis, the provision for credit losses for the fourth quarter of 2025 was $6.78&#160;million. The provision for credit losses for the first quarter of 2025 included provision expense of $18.73&#160;million recorded for purchased <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-PCD</span> loans from Piedmont. United&#8217;s provision for credit losses relates to its portfolio of loans and leases, <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">available-for-sale</span></span> securities and <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">held-to-maturity</span></span> securities are discussed in more detail in the following paragraphs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the quarter ended March&#160;31, 2026, the provision for loan and lease losses was $7.78&#160;million as compared to a provision for loan and lease losses of $29.10&#160;million for the quarter ended March&#160;31, 2025. The lower amount of provision expense for the first quarter of 2026 compared to the first quarter of 2025 was mainly due to the previously mentioned provision expense of $18.73&#160;million recorded for purchased <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-PCD</span> loans from Piedmont during the first quarter of 2025. Net charge-offs were $5.70&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 compared to net charge-offs of $8.04&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. The lower amount of net charge-offs for 2026 as compared to 2025 was primarily due to decreased charge-offs within the consumer and other commercial loan segments. On a linked-quarter basis, the provision for loan and lease losses for the fourth quarter of 2025 was $6.78&#160;million. Net charge-offs were $9.31&#160;million for the fourth quarter of 2025. Annualized net charge-offs as a percentage of average loans and leases, net of unearned income for the first quarter of 2026 was 0.15% as compared to annualized net charge-offs of 0.14% for the first quarter of 2025 and annualized net charge-offs of 0.15% for the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table shows a summary of United&#8217;s nonperforming assets including nonperforming loans and other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) at March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United maintains an allowance for loan and lease losses and a reserve for lending-related commitments. The combined allowance for loan losses and reserve for lending-related commitments is considered the allowance for credit losses. At March&#160;31, 2026, the allowance for credit losses was $336.65&#160;million as compared to $332.59&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At March&#160;31, 2026, the allowance for loan and lease losses was $299.60&#160;million as compared to $297.52&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2025. The allowance for loan and lease losses at March&#160;31, 2026 saw the largest increase in the reserves for the commercial real estate nonowner-occupied loan segment from <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> 2025 due to increased outstanding loan balances and an increased adjustment resulting from the reasonable and supportable forecast around economic and business conditions. The largest decrease in reserves at March&#160;31, 2026 was for the real estate construction and development loan segment due to a decreased adjustment within the reasonable and supportable forecast around strength and growth of the segment. As a percentage of loans and leases, net of unearned income, the allowance for loan and lease losses was 1.20% at both March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025. The ratio of the allowance for loan and lease losses to nonperforming loans and leases or coverage ratio was 291.34% and 293.22% at March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, respectively. The slight decrease in this ratio was due mainly to a larger increase in nonperforming loans as compared to the increase in the allowance for loan and lease losses. </p>

Reserves are initially determined based on losses identified from the PD/LGD and Cohort models which utilize the Company&#8217;s historical information. Then, any qualitative adjustments are applied to account for the Company&#8217;s view of the future and other factors. If current conditions underlying any qualitative adjustment factor were deemed to be materially different than historical conditions, an adjustment was made for that factor. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The first quarter of 2026 qualitative adjustments include analyses of the following: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;text-align:left">Reversion to historical loss data occurs via a straight-line method during the year following the <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-year</span> reasonable and supportable forecast period. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s review of the allowance for loan and lease losses at March&#160;31, 2026 produced increased reserves in two of the four loan categories as compared to December&#160;31, 2025. The allowance related to the commercial, financial&#160;&amp; agricultural loan pool, consisting of the owner and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-owner</span> occupied commercial real estate and other commercial loan segments, increased $5.75&#160;million due to increased outstanding loan balances. The consumer loan segment reserve increased $738&#160;thousand primarily due to an increase in the quarterly maximum loss experience utilized within the reasonable and supportable forecast adjustment. The real estate construction and development loan segment reserve decreased $4.09&#160;million due to improvement in the reasonable and supportable adjustment. The residential real estate loan segment reserve decreased $319&#160;thousand due to an improvement in historical loss rates. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">An allowance is established for estimated lifetime losses for loans that are individually assessed. Nonperforming commercial loans and leases are regularly reviewed to identify expected credit losses. A loan is individually assessed for expected credit losses when the loan does not share similar characteristics with other loans in the portfolio. Measuring expected credit losses of a loan requires judgment and estimates, and the eventual outcomes may differ from those estimates. Expected credit losses are measured based upon the present value of expected future cash flows from the loan discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective rate or the fair value of collateral if the loan is collateral dependent. When the selected measure is less than the recorded investment in the loan, an expected credit loss has occurred. The allowance for loans and leases that were individually assessed was $10.60&#160;million at March&#160;31, 2026 and $8.04&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2025. In comparison to <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end,</span> this element of the allowance increased $2.57&#160;million due to collateral weaknesses identified in several relationships which necessitated individually assessed reserves and increases to reserves previously identified. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">68 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Management believes that the allowance for credit losses of $336.65&#160;million at March&#160;31, 2026 is appropriate to provide for expected losses on existing loans and lending-related commitments based on information currently available. United&#8217;s loan administration policies are focused on the risk characteristics of the loan portfolio in terms of loan approval and credit quality. The commercial loan portfolio is monitored for possible concentrations of credit in one or more industries. Management has lending limits as a percentage of capital per type of credit concentration in an effort to ensure adequate diversification within the portfolio. Most of United&#8217;s commercial loans are secured by real estate located in United&#8217;s footprint. It is the opinion of management that these commercial loans do not pose any unusual risks and that adequate consideration has been given to these loans in establishing the allowance for credit losses. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The provision for credit losses related to held to maturity securities for the first quarter of 2026 and 2025 was immaterial. The allowance for credit losses related to held to maturity securities was $16&#160;thousand as of March&#160;31, 2026 as well as December&#160;31, 2025. There was no provision for credit losses recorded on available for sale investment securities for the first quarter of 2026 and 2025 and no allowance for credit losses on available for sale investment securities as of March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Management is not aware of any potential problem loans or leases, trends or uncertainties, which it reasonably expects, will materially impact future operating results, liquidity, or capital resources which have not been disclosed. Additionally, management has disclosed all known material credits, which cause management to have serious doubts as to the ability of such borrowers to comply with the loan repayment schedules. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Other Income </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other income consists of all revenues, which are not included in interest and fee income related to earning assets. Noninterest income has been and will continue to be an important factor for improving United&#8217;s profitability. Recognizing the importance, management continues to evaluate areas where noninterest income can be enhanced. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Noninterest income for the first quarter of 2026 was $34.06&#160;million, an increase of $4.51&#160;million or 15.26% from the first quarter of 2025. This increase was driven by increases in fees from brokerage services and net gains on investment securities. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Fees from brokerage services for the first quarter of 2026 increased $1.76&#160;million or 31.14% from the first quarter of 2025 due to higher volume driven by growth in the business. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Net gains on investment securities were $2.27&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to net gains on investment securities were $521&#160;thousand for the first quarter of 2025. The net gains on investment securities in the first quarter of 2026 were primarily due to a net gain on the sale of equity securities whereas the net gains on investment securities in the first quarter of 2025 were due to an increase in the fair value of equity securities. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On a linked-quarter basis, noninterest income for the first quarter of 2026 increased of $3.13&#160;million, or 10.11%, from the fourth quarter of 2025. Net gains on investment securities were $2.27&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to net losses on investment securities of $218&#160;thousand for the fourth quarter of 2025. Net gains on investment securities for the first quarter of 2026 were primarily due to the above mentioned gains on sales of equity securities. Fees from brokerage services increased $1.45&#160;million from the fourth quarter of 2025, primarily due to previously mentioned higher volume driven by growth in the business. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Other Expenses </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Just as management continues to evaluate areas where noninterest income can be enhanced, it strives to improve the efficiency of its operations to reduce costs. Other expenses include all items of expense other than interest expense, the provision for credit losses, and income taxes. Noninterest expense for the first quarter of 2026 was $152.81&#160;million which was relatively flat from the first quarter of 2025, decreasing $759&#160;thousand or less than 1%. The first quarter of 2025 included $11.31&#160;million of merger-rated expenses from the Piedmont acquisition. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">69 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Employee compensation for the first quarter of 2026 increased $2.63&#160;million or 4.32% when compared to the first quarter of 2025. The increase in employee compensation was primarily due to higher employee incentives and higher brokerage commissions. Employee compensation for the first quarter of 2025 included $1.17&#160;million in merger-related expenses. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Employee benefits expense for the first quarter of 2026 increased $2.69&#160;million or 20.23% from the first quarter of 2025. This increase in employee benefits was primarily due to higher post-retirement benefit and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (&#8220;FICA&#8221;) costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Data processing expense for the first quarter of 2026 decreased $1.45&#160;million or 17.20% from the first quarter of 2025. The decrease in data processing was primarily due to technology contract renegotiations. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other expense for the first quarter of 2026 decreased $5.43&#160;million or 12.21% from the first quarter of 2025. Within other expense for the first quarter of 2026, merger-related expenses decreased $6.00&#160;million and consulting fees declined $2.93&#160;million from the first quarter of 2025. These decreases within other expense were partially offset by increases of $873&#160;thousand in the amortization of investment tax credits and $811&#160;thousand in business franchise taxes. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On a linked-quarter basis, noninterest expense for the first quarter of 2026 was relatively flat from the fourth quarter of 2025, increasing $1.10&#160;million, or less than 1%. An increase in employee benefits of $3.01&#160;million and an increase in Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) insurance expense of $1.06&#160;million was mostly offset by a $1.08&#160;million decrease in data processing expense and a $1.79&#160;million decrease in other expense. The increase in employee benefits was primarily due to higher FICA and post-retirement benefit costs. FDIC insurance expense for the fourth quarter of 2025 included a $1.2&#160;million reduction of expense reflecting the FDIC&#8217;s reduced estimates related to the special assessment. The decrease in data processing was primarily due to the previously mentioned technology contract renegotiations. Within other expense, the amortization of investment tax credits declined $920&#160;thousand. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Income Taxes </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the first quarter of 2026, income tax expense was $31.79&#160;million as compared to $22.63&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. The increase of $9.16&#160;million was primarily due to higher earnings partially offset by a lower effective tax rate. On a linked-quarter basis, income tax expense increased $720&#160;thousand primarily due to a higher effective tax rate partially offset by lower earnings. United&#8217;s effective tax rate was 20.38% for the first quarter of 2026, 21.16% for the first quarter of 2025 and 19.43% for the fourth quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Liquidity and Capital Resources </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the opinion of management, United maintains liquidity that is sufficient to satisfy its depositors&#8217; requirements and the credit needs of its customers. Like all banks, United depends upon its ability to renew maturing deposits and other liabilities on a daily basis and to acquire new funds in a variety of markets. A significant source of funds available to United is &#8220;core deposits&#8221;. Core deposits include certain demand deposits, statement and special savings and NOW accounts. These deposits are relatively stable, and they are the lowest cost source of funds available to United. Short-term borrowings have also been a significant source of funds. These include federal funds purchased and securities sold under agreements to repurchase as well as advances from the FHLB. Repurchase agreements represent funds which are obtained as the result of a competitive bidding process. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Liquid assets are cash and those items readily convertible to cash. All banks must maintain sufficient balances of cash and near-cash items to meet the <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</span></span> demands of customers and United&#8217;s cash needs. Other than cash and due from banks, the available for sale securities portfolio and maturing loans are the primary sources of liquidity. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">70 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The goal of liquidity management is to ensure the ability to access funding which enables United to efficiently satisfy the cash flow requirements of depositors and borrowers and meet United&#8217;s cash needs. Liquidity is managed by monitoring funds&#8217; availability from a number of primary sources. Substantial funding is available from cash and cash equivalents, unused short-term borrowing and a geographically dispersed network of branches providing access to a diversified and substantial retail deposit market. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Short-term needs can be met through a wide array of outside sources such as correspondent and downstream correspondent federal funds and utilization of Federal Home Loan Bank advances. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Other sources of liquidity available to United to provide long-term as well as short-term funding alternatives, in addition to FHLB advances, are long-term certificates of deposit, lines of credit, borrowings that are secured by bank premises or stock of United&#8217;s subsidiaries and issuances of trust preferred securities. In the normal course of business, United through its Asset Liability Committee evaluates these as well as other alternative funding strategies that may be utilized to meet short-term and long-term funding needs. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During the first quarter of 2026, United decreased its interest-bearing deposit balance at the FRB by $264.52&#160;million to $1.97&#160;billion. The change in the balance at the FRB was mostly the result of growth in loans of $154.34&#160;million, net purchases of $164.18&#160;million in available for sale debt securities and a net repayment of $32.40&#160;million in securities sold under agreements to repurchase partially offset by a growth in total deposits of $59.95&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, cash of $160.86&#160;million was provided by operating activities due mainly to net income of $124.20&#160;million. In addition, proceeds from the sale of mortgage loans in the secondary market exceeded originations by $4.60&#160;million and the provision for loan losses was $7.78&#160;million for the first quarter. Net cash of $304.11&#160;million was used in investing activities which was primarily due to loan growth of $154.34&#160;million and net purchases of investment securities of $145.46&#160;million over proceeds from sales. During the first three months of 2026, net cash of $93.96&#160;million was used in financing activities due primarily to net acquisition of $70.26&#160;million in treasury stock, cash dividends paid of $53.38&#160;million and the net repayment of securities sold under agreements to repurchase of $32.40&#160;million partially offset by growth in deposits of $59.95&#160;million. The net effect of the cash flow activities was a decrease in cash and cash equivalents of $237.22&#160;million for the first three months of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At March&#160;31, 2026, United had an unused borrowing amount at the FHLB of approximately $9.24&#160;billion subject to delivery of collateral after certain trigger points and $4.89&#160;billion without the delivery of additional collateral. United has various unused lines of credit available from certain of its correspondent banks in the aggregate amount of $280&#160;million, all of which was available at March&#160;31, 2026. At March&#160;31, 2026, United&#8217;s borrowing capacity for the FRB Discount Window was $4.59&#160;billion. United did not have any borrowings from the FRB&#8217;s Discount Window during the first quarter of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United anticipates it can meet its obligations over the next 12 months and has no material commitments for capital expenditures. United also has lines of credit available. See Notes 8 and 9 to the accompanying unaudited Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for more details regarding the amounts available to United under lines of credit. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Asset Liability Committee monitors liquidity to ascertain that a liquidity position within certain prescribed parameters is maintained. No changes are anticipated in the policies of United&#8217;s Asset Liability Committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s capital position is financially sound. United seeks to maintain a proper relationship between capital and total assets to support growth and sustain earnings. United has historically generated attractive returns on shareholders&#8217; equity. United is well-capitalized based upon regulatory guidelines. United&#8217;s risk-based capital ratio is 15.54% at March&#160;31, 2026 while its Common Equity Tier 1 capital, Tier 1 capital and leverage ratios are 13.27%, 13.27% and 11.24%, respectively. The regulatory requirements for a well-capitalized financial institution are a risk-based capital ratio of 10.0%, a Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 6.5%, a Tier 1 capital ratio of 8.0% and a leverage ratio of 5.0%. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">71 </p>

<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Total shareholders&#8217; equity was $5.49&#160;billion at March&#160;31, 2026, which was a relatively flat from December&#160;31, 2025, decreasing $7.86&#160;million or less than 1%. This slight decrease was primarily due to a decrease of $10.19&#160;million in accumulated other comprehensive loss and an increase of $70.91&#160;million in treasury stock. During the first quarter of 2026, United repurchased 1,739,501 shares of its common stock at an average price of $39.92 per share. Partially offsetting these decreases to shareholders&#8217; equity was an increase of $71.03&#160;million in retained earnings as a result of net earnings (net income less dividends declared) during the first quarter of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s shareholders&#8217; equity to assets ratio was 16.28% at March&#160;31, 2026 as compared to 16.33% at December&#160;31, 2025. The primary capital ratio, capital and reserves to total assets and reserves, was 17.11% at March&#160;31, 2026 as compared to 17.15% at December&#160;31, 2025. United&#8217;s average shareholders&#8217; equity to average asset ratio was 16.45% for the first quarter of 2026 as compared to 16.42% the first quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">During the first quarter of 2026, United&#8217;s Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $0.38 per share. Total cash dividends declared were $53.17&#160;million for the first quarter of 2026 which was relatively flat from dividends declared of $53.34&#160;million for the first quarter of 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="toc51730_10">Item&#8201;3. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The objective of United&#8217;s Asset Liability Management function is to maintain consistent growth in net interest income within United&#8217;s policy guidelines. This objective is accomplished through the management of balance sheet liquidity and interest rate risk exposures due to changes in economic conditions, interest rate levels and customer preferences. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Interest Rate Risk </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Management considers interest rate risk to be United&#8217;s most significant market risk. Interest rate risk is the exposure to adverse changes in United&#8217;s net interest income as a result of changes in interest rates. United&#8217;s earnings are largely dependent on the effective management of interest rate risk. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Management of interest rate risk focuses on maintaining consistent growth in net interest income within Board-approved policy limits. United&#8217;s Asset/Liability Management Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;), which includes senior management representatives and reports to the Board of Directors, monitors and manages interest rate risk to maintain an acceptable level of change to net interest income as a result of changes in interest rates. Policy established for interest rate risk is stated in terms of the change in net interest income over a <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-year</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-year</span> horizon given an immediate and sustained increase or decrease in interest rates. The current limits approved by the Board of Directors are structured on a staged basis with each stage requiring specific actions. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United employs a variety of measurement techniques to identify and manage its exposure to changing interest rates. One such technique utilizes an earnings simulation model to analyze the sensitivity of net interest income to movements in interest rates. The model is based on actual cash flows and repricing characteristics for on and <span style="white-space:nowrap">off-balance</span> sheet instruments and incorporates market-based assumptions regarding the impact of changing interest rates on the prepayment rate of certain assets and liabilities. The model also includes executive management projections for activity levels in product lines offered by United. Assumptions based on the historical behavior of deposit rates and balances in relation to changes in interest rates are also incorporated into the model. Rate scenarios could involve parallel or nonparallel shifts in the yield curve, depending on historical, current, and expected conditions, as well as the need to capture any material effects of explicit or embedded options. These assumptions are inherently uncertain and, as a result, the model cannot precisely measure net interest income or precisely predict the impact of fluctuations in interest rates on net interest income. Actual results will differ from simulated results due to timing, magnitude and frequency of interest rate changes as well as changes in market conditions and management&#8217;s strategies. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">72 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Interest sensitive assets and liabilities are defined as those assets or liabilities that mature or are repriced within a designated time frame. The principal function of managing interest rate risk is to maintain an appropriate relationship between those assets and liabilities that are sensitive to changing market interest rates. The difference between rate sensitive assets and rate sensitive liabilities for specified periods of time is known as the &#8220;GAP.&#8221; Earnings-simulation analysis captures not only the potential of these interest sensitive assets and liabilities to mature or reprice, but also the probability that they will do so. Moreover, earnings-simulation analysis considers the relative sensitivities of these balance sheet items and projects their behavior over an extended period of time. United closely monitors the sensitivity of its assets and liabilities on an <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-going</span> basis and projects the effect of various interest rate changes on its net interest margin. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table shows United&#8217;s estimated earnings sensitivity profile as of March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At March&#160;31, 2026, given an immediate, sustained 100 basis point upward shock to the yield curve used in the simulation model, net interest income for United is estimated to increase by 2.48% over one year as compared to an increase by 2.31% at December&#160;31, 2025. A 200 basis point immediate, sustained upward shock in the yield curve would increase net interest income by an estimated 4.23% over one year as of March&#160;31, 2026, as compared to an increase of 3.85% as of December&#160;31, 2025. A 100 basis point immediate, sustained downward shock in the yield curve would increase net interest income by an estimated 0.01% over one year as of March&#160;31, 2026 as compared to an increase of 0.20% over one year as of December&#160;31, 2025. A 200 basis point immediate, sustained downward shock in the yield curve would increase net interest income by an estimated 1.36% over one year as of March&#160;31, 2026 as compared to an increase of 1.58% over one year as of December&#160;31, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition to the one year earnings sensitivity analysis, a <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-year</span> analysis is also performed. Compared to the one year analysis, United is projected to show improved performance in year two within the upward rate shock scenarios. Given an immediate, sustained 100 basis point upward shock to the yield curve used in the simulation model, net interest income for United is estimated to increase by 4.57% in year two as of March&#160;31, 2026. A 200 basis point immediate, sustained upward shock in the yield curve would increase net interest income by an estimated 8.14% in year two as of March&#160;31, 2026. A 100 basis point immediate, sustained downward shock in the yield curve would decrease net interest income by an estimated 2.74% in year two as of March&#160;31, 2026. A 200 basis point immediate, sustained downward shock in the yield curve would decrease net interest income by an estimated 4.94% in year two as of March&#160;31, 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">While it is unlikely market rates would immediately move 100 or 200 basis points upward or downward on a sustained basis, this is another tool used by management and the Board to gauge interest rate risk. All of these estimated changes in net interest income are and were within the policy guidelines established by the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To further aid in interest rate management, United&#8217;s subsidiary bank is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;). The use of FHLB advances provides United with a low risk means of matching maturities of earning assets and interest-bearing funds to achieve a desired interest rate spread over the life of the earning assets. In addition, United uses credit with large regional banks and trust preferred securities to provide funding. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As part of its interest rate risk management strategy, United may use derivative instruments to protect against adverse price or interest rate movements on the value of certain assets or liabilities and on future cash flows. These derivatives commonly consist of interest rate swaps, caps, floors, collars, futures, forward contracts, written and purchased options. Interest rate swaps obligate two parties to exchange one or more payments generally calculated with reference to a fixed or variable rate of interest applied to the notional amount. United accounts for its derivative activities in accordance with the provisions of ASC Topic 815. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">73 </p>

<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Extension Risk </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At March&#160;31, 2026, United&#8217;s mortgage related securities portfolio had an amortized cost of $2.1&#160;billion, of which approximately $1.2&#160;billion or 58% were fixed rate collateralized mortgage obligations (&#8220;CMOs&#8221;). These fixed rate CMOs consisted primarily of planned amortization class (&#8220;PACs&#8221;), <span style="white-space:nowrap">sequential-pay</span> and accretion directed (&#8220;VADMs&#8221;) bonds having an average life of approximately 3.9 years and a weighted average yield of 3.55%, under current projected prepayment assumptions. These securities are expected to have moderate extension risk in a rising rate environment. Current models show that given an immediate, sustained upward shock of 300 basis points, the average life of these securities would only extend to 5.8 years. The projected price decline of the fixed rate CMO portfolio in rates up 300 basis points would be 14%, or less than the price decline of a <span style="white-space:nowrap">5-year</span> treasury note. By comparison, the price decline of a <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-year</span> 5% current coupon mortgage backed security (&#8220;MBS&#8221;) in rates higher by 300 basis points would be approximately 21%. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United had approximately $335.5&#160;million in fixed rate Commercial mortgage backed Securities (&#8220;CMBS&#8221;) with a projected yield of 1.94% and a projected average life of 3.9 years on March&#160;31, 2026. This portfolio consisted primarily of Freddie Mac Multifamily K securities and Fannie Mae Delegated Underwriting and Servicing (&#8220;DUS&#8221;) securities with a weighted average maturity (&#8220;WAM&#8221;) of 8.5 years. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United had approximately $19&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">15-year</span> mortgage backed securities with a projected yield of 4.01% and a projected average life of 3.7 years as of March&#160;31, 2026. This portfolio consisted of seasoned <span style="white-space:nowrap">15-year</span> mortgage paper with a weighted average loan age (&#8220;WALA&#8221;) of 6 years and a WAM of 9.2 years. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United had approximately $288.5&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">20-year</span> mortgage backed securities with a projected yield of 2.15% and a projected average life of 5.5 years on March&#160;31, 2026. This portfolio consisted of seasoned <span style="white-space:nowrap">20-year</span> mortgage paper with a WALA of 5 years and a WAM of 14.7 years. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United had approximately $204.9&#160;million in <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-year</span> mortgage backed securities with a projected yield of 3.91% and a projected average life of 7 years on March&#160;31, 2026. This portfolio consisted of seasoned <span style="white-space:nowrap">30-year</span> mortgage paper with a WALA of 6.4 years and a WAM of 22.2 years. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The remaining 2% of the mortgage related securities portfolio on March&#160;31, 2026, included floating rate CMO, CMBS and mortgage backed securities. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="toc51730_11">Item&#8201;4. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of March&#160;31, 2026, an evaluation was performed under the supervision of and with the participation of United&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), of the effectiveness of the design and operation of United&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures. Based on that evaluation, United&#8217;s management, including the CEO and CFO, concluded that United&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures as of March&#160;31, 2026 were effective in ensuring that information required to be disclosed in the Quarterly Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-Q</span> was recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time period required by the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Limitations on the Effectiveness of Controls </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">United&#8217;s management, including the CEO and CFO, does not expect that United&#8217;s disclosure controls and internal controls will prevent all errors and fraud. While United&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures are designed to provide reasonable assurance of achieving their objective, a control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met. Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within the Company have been detected. These inherent limitations include the realities that judgments in decision-making can be faulty, and that breakdowns can occur because of simple error or mistake. Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people, or by management override of the controls. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Changes in Internal Controls </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">There have been no changes in United&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules <span style="white-space:nowrap">13a-15(e)</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">15d-15(f)</span> under the Exchange Act) that occurred during the quarter ended March&#160;31, 2026, or in other factors that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect United&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. </p>
